# Commands reference

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask gen-docs`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every operation is a JSON object whose `type` is the operation name, followed by its parameters, e.g.

```json
{"type": "panel.create_rect", "width": 500, "height": 700}
```

IDs are strings such as `"panel:2"`. Lengths are in millimetres.
Errors are structured: a stable `code`, named `args` and an English `text`.

## Script steps

A script (CLI `r3d run`) is a JSON array of steps. A step is a command, a query, or one of:

- `{"type": "history.undo"}`: undo the last step.
- `{"type": "history.redo"}`: redo the last undone step.
- `{"type": "history.list"}`: the steps of the history, oldest first (`steps`, each with its `label`: the command's name, or the batch's), and how many are done (`at`).
- `{"type": "history.go_to", "at": 3}`: undo or redo until `at` steps are done (0 undoes them all).
- `{"type": "batch", "label": "...", "commands": [...]}`: run commands atomically as one undo step, named `label` in the history (optional, default `batch`); if one fails, none is applied.

Undo, redo and go-to return the panels they changed (`panels`); the app selects them.

A string such as `"$3.created[0]"` refers to the result of an earlier step (step 3, 0-based, then the path `.created[0]`; `[n]` indexes arrays, `.name` reads fields). It must be the whole string; `$$` writes a literal `$`. References keep scripts independent of ID allocation.

## Commands

Document edits. Every command can be undone.

### `avatar.set`

Set the avatar's body. The measurements go inside `body`, not at the top level: {"body": {"masculinity": 0, "height_cm": 168, "bust_cm": 92, "waist_cm": 74, "hips_cm": 100}}; masculinity 0 feminine – 1 masculine, the rest in cm, and for a child `age_years` (0–18; left out: an adult). `preset` only records which preset the body came from: to use one, copy its `body` from avatar.presets. The 3D body is fitted to these measurements, with a child's proportions at that age; avatar.get reports what it actually measures.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "Body": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "Body measurements (cm), the input of the avatar fitting.",
      "properties": {
        "age_years": {
          "description": "A child's age in years ([`Body::AGE_RANGE`]); absent for an\nadult.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "bust_cm": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "height_cm": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "hips_cm": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "masculinity": {
          "description": "0 = feminine body, 1 = masculine body.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "waist_cm": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "masculinity",
        "height_cm",
        "bust_cm",
        "waist_cm",
        "hips_cm"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Set the avatar's measurements.",
  "properties": {
    "body": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Body",
      "description": "The measurements: `masculinity` (0 = feminine body, 1 =\nmasculine), `height_cm`, `bust_cm`, `waist_cm`, `hips_cm`, and\n`age_years` for a child."
    },
    "preset": {
      "description": "Name of the preset the measurements come from, if any (a label:\nthe body is still given in `body`).",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "body"
  ],
  "title": "AvatarSet",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `avatar.set_measures`

Set the avatar's other measurements in cm by name: neck, shoulder_width, shoulder_length, back_waist_length, front_waist_length, waist_height, hip_height, crotch_depth (torso); arm_length, upper_arm, wrist (arms); inside_leg, thigh, knee, ankle (legs). Null goes back to the estimate from height, bust, waist and hips. The 3D body follows the ones it can (avatar.get says which and what it reaches); formulas and templates use them all, each size of a range graded like its estimate.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Set or reset the avatar's other measurements (spec 29).",
  "properties": {
    "measures": {
      "additionalProperties": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": [
          "number",
          "null"
        ]
      },
      "description": "By name (`neck`, `arm_length`…): the value in cm, or null to go\nback to the estimate.",
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "measures"
  ],
  "title": "AvatarSetMeasures",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `avatar.import_mesh`

Drape on a body read from a file in the project folder (run `avatar.import`, which reads the file and calls this). Units, up axis and facing are detected unless given; the arrangement points are guessed and the measurements taken on the body (templates are sized from them).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "UpAxis": {
      "description": "An axis of a model file.",
      "enum": [
        "y",
        "z",
        "x",
        "-y",
        "-z",
        "-x"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Drape on a body imported from a file already read (`avatar.import`\nreads it; an agent calls that action rather than this command).",
  "properties": {
    "file": {
      "description": "The file, relative to the project folder (`avatars/scan.glb`).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "hash": {
      "description": "Its fingerprint, as `avatar.import` returns it.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "scale": {
      "description": "Metres per file unit; detected when omitted.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "turn_deg": {
      "description": "Turn about the vertical (degrees) so the body faces +Z; detected\nwhen omitted.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "up": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/UpAxis"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The file's up axis; detected when omitted."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "file",
    "hash"
  ],
  "title": "AvatarImportMesh",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `avatar.orient`

Correct how the imported body's file is read: its units (scale, metres per unit), which axis is up, and a turn about the vertical so it faces +Z. Omitted values stay. The arrangement points are guessed again and the measurements taken again.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "UpAxis": {
      "description": "An axis of a model file.",
      "enum": [
        "y",
        "z",
        "x",
        "-y",
        "-z",
        "-x"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Correct the units, up axis or facing of the imported body.",
  "properties": {
    "scale": {
      "description": "Metres per file unit (0.01 for centimetres, 0.001 for millimetres,\n0.0254 for inches).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "turn_deg": {
      "description": "Turn about the vertical (degrees) so the body faces +Z.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "up": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/UpAxis"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The file's axis that points up: `y`, `z`, `x`, `-y`, `-z`, `-x`."
    }
  },
  "title": "AvatarOrient",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `avatar.set_point`

Move an arrangement point of the imported body (mm, Y up, facing +Z, the body's left at +x): chest, waist, hips (the measurements are taken again at their height), crotch, left/right_shoulder, _elbow, _wrist (the axis sleeves wrap around), left/right_thigh, _shin (the trouser legs' axis). A point must lie inside the body; avatar.check flags it otherwise.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "BodyPoint": {
      "description": "Points that tell the drape where the body's parts are (spec 27).",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "enum": [
            "left_shoulder",
            "left_elbow",
            "left_wrist",
            "right_shoulder",
            "right_elbow",
            "right_wrist",
            "right_thigh",
            "right_shin"
          ],
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "chest",
          "description": "The middle of the torso at the bust or chest girth.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "waist",
          "description": "The middle of the torso at the waist girth.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "hips",
          "description": "The middle of the torso at the hips girth.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "crotch",
          "description": "Where the legs part.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "left_thigh",
          "description": "The middle of the left thigh: the top of the left leg's axis.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "left_shin",
          "description": "The middle of the left shin: the axis goes through it.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Move one arrangement point of the imported body.",
  "properties": {
    "at_mm": {
      "description": "Where (mm, Y up, the body facing +Z, its left at +x, feet at 0).",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 3,
      "minItems": 3,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "point": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/BodyPoint"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "point",
    "at_mm"
  ],
  "title": "AvatarSetPoint",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `object.set`

Make the project an object rather than a garment worn (a bag, a cushion, a toy): it has no body (the avatar and its measurements are removed), and in 3D it is weightless, so the cloth keeps the shape its seams give it instead of falling in folds; the parts closed all around are stuffed by `stuffing` (0 none – 1 firm, default 0.5; open parts never are). Again on an object, it changes the stuffing. object.clear makes it a garment again.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Make the project an object, or change its stuffing.",
  "properties": {
    "stuffing": {
      "description": "How firmly the parts closed all around are stuffed: 0 none, 1\nfirm. Left out: as it is, or 0.5 for a project becoming an object.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ObjectSet",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `object.clear`

Make an object project a garment worn again: weight comes back in 3D; give it a body with avatar.set.

### `panel.create_rect`

Create a rectangular panel. Returns the panel, then its 4 points (counter-clockwise from the origin), then its 4 edges.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Create a rectangular panel.",
  "properties": {
    "grain_angle_deg": {
      "default": 90.0,
      "description": "Grainline angle in degrees from +X. Defaults to 90 (vertical).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "height": {
      "description": "Height in mm (> 0).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "Panel name. Defaults to \"Panel N\".",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "origin": {
      "default": [
        0.0,
        0.0
      ],
      "description": "Bottom-left corner on the board, in mm. Defaults to `[0, 0]`.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "width": {
      "description": "Width in mm (> 0).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "width",
    "height"
  ],
  "title": "PanelCreateRect",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.create_polygon`

Create a panel from a closed polygon. With `symmetric`, the points draw half a piece against an axis, the closing edge: the other half follows (panel.unfold). Returns the panel, then its points, then its edges (then, symmetric, the reflected half's points and edges).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Create a panel from a closed polygon.",
  "properties": {
    "grain_angle_deg": {
      "default": 90.0,
      "description": "Grainline angle in degrees from +X. Defaults to 90 (vertical).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "Panel name. Defaults to \"Panel N\".",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "points": {
      "description": "At least 3 vertices in mm; the closing edge is implicit. Must form a\nsimple outline (no crossing or overlapping edges). Stored\ncounter-clockwise.",
      "items": {
        "items": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "maxItems": 2,
        "minItems": 2,
        "type": "array"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "symmetric": {
      "description": "The points draw half a piece: the closing edge, from the last point\nback to the first, is its axis, and the piece is unfolded across it\n(as panel.unfold does).",
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "points"
  ],
  "title": "PanelCreatePolygon",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.create_path`

Create a panel from a closed path of straight and cubic Bézier edges (mm), like internal_line.add but closed. Must form a simple outline; stored counter-clockwise. With `symmetric`, the path draws half a piece against an axis, the straight edge back to `start`: the other half follows (panel.unfold). Returns the panel, then its points, then its edges (then, symmetric, the reflected half's points and edges).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "SegmentSpec": {
      "description": "One segment of an internal line, starting where the previous one ended.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "line",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "to": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {
            "c1": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "c2": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "cubic",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "to": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "c1",
            "c2",
            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Create a panel from a closed path of straight and curved edges.",
  "properties": {
    "grain_angle_deg": {
      "default": 90.0,
      "description": "Grainline angle in degrees from +X. Defaults to 90 (vertical).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "Panel name. Defaults to \"Panel N\".",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "segments": {
      "description": "The edges in order, each starting where the previous one ended. The\nlast one should end at `start`; if it does not, a straight edge\ncloses the outline.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/SegmentSpec"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "start": {
      "description": "First point of the outline (mm).",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "symmetric": {
      "description": "The path draws half a piece: the straight edge back to `start` is\nits axis, and the piece is unfolded across it (as panel.unfold\ndoes).",
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "start",
    "segments"
  ],
  "title": "PanelCreatePath",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.rotate`

Turn a whole panel on the board by an angle (degrees, counter-clockwise), about a point (default: the centre of its bounding box). Its lines, pins, buttons, grainline and print turn with it; horizontal and vertical constraints swap on a quarter turn, and any other angle is refused while the panel has them. Not on a linked mirror copy (turn its source).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Turn a whole panel on the board.",
  "properties": {
    "angle_deg": {
      "description": "Degrees, counter-clockwise on the board (+X towards +Y).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "centre": {
      "description": "The point turned about (mm). Defaults to the centre of the panel's\nbounding box.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    }
  },

### `panel.scale`

Scale a whole panel on the board by a factor across and one up and down (> 0), about a point (default: the centre of its bounding box). Its lines, pins and buttons follow; its dimensions are scaled with it. Refused while a dimension has a formula, or when the two factors differ and a length, a straight distance, an angle or a right angle would no longer hold. Not on a linked mirror copy (scale its source).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Scale a whole panel on the board.",
  "properties": {
    "centre": {
      "description": "The point that stays put (mm). Defaults to the centre of the panel's\nbounding box.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "factor": {
      "description": "Factors across (x) and up and down (y), > 0; `[1.1, 1.1]` makes the\npanel 10 % bigger every way.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel",
    "factor"
  ],
  "title": "PanelScale",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.mirror`

Create a linked mirror copy of a panel (e.g. left/right pieces). The copy follows every later change of its source; move it with panel.translate, or make it independent with panel.unlink. Returns the copy, then its points, then its edges.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Create a linked mirror copy of a panel.",
  "properties": {
    "axis_dir": {
      "description": "Direction of the mirror axis. Defaults to vertical `[0, 1]`.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "axis_origin": {
      "description": "A point on the mirror axis (mm). Defaults to a vertical axis placed\nso the copy sits to the right of the source with a 50 mm gap.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "Name of the copy. Defaults to \"<source name> (mirror)\".",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel"
  ],
  "title": "PanelMirror",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.place`

Place a panel around the body (or around an arm, for sleeves) for the 3D simulation: angle (0 front, 90 left side, 180 back, 270 right side; around an arm 0 is its outside), height of its top in cm, distance from the body in mm. Unplaced panels are not simulated.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "Around": {
      "description": "What a panel is wrapped around when the simulation starts.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "body",
          "description": "The torso and legs: a vertical cylinder around the body's axis.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "left_arm",
          "description": "The left arm (the body's left, +x): wrapped around the upper arm,\nthen the forearm past the elbow.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "right_arm",
          "description": "The right arm (−x).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "left_leg",
          "description": "The left leg (+x), like a trouser leg: wrapped around the leg's\naxis, and above the crotch around the body's left half.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "right_leg",
          "description": "The right leg (−x).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "flat",
          "description": "Not wrapped: a flat sheet facing outward at the placement angle,\n`offset_mm` from the body's vertical axis (a bag hanging in front\nof the body).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Place a panel around the body for the simulation.",
  "properties": {
    "angle_deg": {
      "description": "Angle around the body (degrees): 0 front, 90 the body's left side,\n180 back, 270 right side. Around an arm: 0 the outside of the arm,\n180 the side facing the body. Around a leg, as around the body,\ncentred on the leg.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "around": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Around",
      "default": "body",
      "description": "What the panel is wrapped around: `body` (default), `left_arm` or\n`right_arm` (sleeves), `left_leg` or `right_leg` (trouser legs:\naround the leg, and above the crotch around that half of the body),\nor `flat` (not wrapped: a flat sheet facing outward, `offset_mm`\nfrom the body's axis)."
    },
    "centre_x_mm": {
      "description": "The pattern abscissa (mm) that goes to the angle. Defaults to the\npanel's horizontal centre; the pieces of a cut panel keep the\nwhole's.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "offset_mm": {
      "default": 30.0,
      "description": "Distance from the body at the start of the simulation (mm,\ndefault 30). Around an arm or a leg a panel starts as a closed tube\ninstead (around a leg, just outside it if the leg is thicker).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    },
    "top_cm": {
      "description": "Height of the panel's top above the floor (cm). Around an arm, the\ntop goes to the arm at that height and the panel runs down the arm.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel",
    "angle_deg",
    "top_cm"
  ],
  "title": "PanelPlace",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.delete`

Delete a panel with its points, edges, notches and internal lines. Linked mirror copies of it become independent. Destructive: requires "confirm": true.

**Destructive**: requires `"confirm": true`.

{

    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel"
  ],
  "title": "PanelDelete",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.cut`

Cut a panel in two along an open path of straight and cubic segments (mm) that crosses its outline exactly twice, its ends outside the panel (without `panel`, the one panel it crosses). The two pieces are sewn together along the cut. The larger piece keeps the panel's ID, its seams and pins; the other is a new panel with the same garment, grain and seam allowance, moved 20 mm away on the board and placed where it was around the body. Notches, internal lines and pins go to the piece they are on; a sewn edge that is cut is split with its partner, and the seam with them. Returns the new panel, then the seams along the cut.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "SegmentSpec": {
      "description": "One segment of an internal line, starting where the previous one ended.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "line",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "to": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {
            "c1": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "c2": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "cubic",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "to": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "c1",
            "c2",
            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Cut a panel in two along a straight or curved line.",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "description": "Name of the new piece. Defaults to the panel's name followed by \" 2\".",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "panel": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The panel to cut. If omitted, the one panel the line crosses."
    },
    "segments": {
      "description": "The cut line's segments; it ends outside the panel too.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/SegmentSpec"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "start": {
      "description": "Start of the cut line (mm), outside the panel.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "start",
    "segments"
  ],
  "title": "PanelCut",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.paste`

Paste pieces copied with panel.copy, under new IDs, with the seams between them, their notches, internal lines, construction details, buttons, zippers, constraints (a dimension keeps its name unless the project has one by that name), grade rules (when the project has the same number of sizes and base size), pins and mirror links. A piece keeps its place around the body unless a piece of the project already starts there (pasted beside its original): then it is left unplaced, with no pins. Returns the new panels, then the new seams.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "GarmentId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a garment, e.g. `garment:1`.",
      "pattern": "^garment:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Paste pieces copied with panel.copy.",
  "properties": {
    "clip": {
      "description": "The clip, as panel.copy returns it."
    },
    "garment": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/GarmentId"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The garment the pieces join. Omitted: the one they were copied\nfrom if this project has it, otherwise the project's first."
    },
    "offset": {
      "description": "How far to move the pieces on the board (mm). Omitted: to the right\nof the project's pieces.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "clip"
  ],
  "title": "PanelPaste",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

Move a contour point to a new position in mm. Curve handles attached to the point move with it. The panel may end up self-intersecting; `panel.get` reports it.

Set the straight-line distance between two contour points (e.g. across the shoulders, or between two pieces' corners): `point` moves along the line from `from` through it, as `point.move` does (its curve handles follow); `from` stays. `measure.distance` gives the current distance.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PointId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a point, e.g. `point:1`.",

      "type": "string"
    }
  },

  "description": "Put a point at a distance from another.",

  "required": [

    "point",
    "distance_mm"
  ],

  "type": "object"
}
```

### `seam.add`

Sew two sides together. A side is a whole `edge`, a run of consecutive outline `edges` of one piece (in order around it), or an internal `line`, each optionally only `from_mm`/`to_mm` along it (a seam between two notches, a pocket sewn on its placement line, the two halves of a pleat on one edge). Points are matched along the sides, start to start unless a side is reversed; leave b.reversed out to have it chosen (an edge and its linked mirror image meet mirrored point to mirrored point; other sides are walked both the same way on the pattern), and use seam.flip if the seam looks twisted. Stretches already sewn cannot be sewn again (invalid.overlaps). `ease_mm` is how much longer side a is meant to be. Returns the seam.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "InternalLineId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a line, e.g. `line:1`.",
      "pattern": "^line:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "SeamSideSpec": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "One side of a new seam: a whole edge, a run of edges, or an internal\nline; all of it or part of it.",
      "properties": {
        "edge": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "One edge."
        },
        "edges": {
          "description": "Or consecutive outline edges of one piece, in their order around it\n(e.g. a pocket's sides and bottom).",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "from_mm": {
          "description": "Only from here along the path (mm from its start). Omitted: its\nstart.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "line": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/InternalLineId"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Or an internal line (a pocket's placement line, a tuck's line)."
        },
        "reversed": {
          "description": "Walk the side from its end instead of its start. Omitted: `false`\nfor side `a`; for side `b`, an edge sewn to its linked mirror image\nmeets it mirrored point to mirrored point (a centre seam), other\nsides are walked both the same way on the pattern (what sewing two\npanels laid side by side needs).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "to_mm": {
          "description": "Only to here (mm from the path's start). Omitted: its end.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Sew two sides together.",
  "properties": {
    "a": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/SeamSideSpec"
    },
    "b": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/SeamSideSpec"
    },
    "ease_mm": {
      "description": "How much longer side `a` is meant to be than `b` (mm, negative:\nshorter), eased in: not reported as a mismatch.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "a",
    "b"
  ],
  "title": "SeamAdd",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "SeamId": {

}
```

</details>

Set a seam's ease: how much longer its side a is meant to be than side b (mm; negative, shorter). The extra length is eased in along the seam when it drapes; only the difference beyond the ease is reported as a mismatch.

      "description": "How much longer side `a` is meant to be than side `b` (mm;\nnegative, shorter): eased in along the seam (a sleeve cap, a back\nshoulder), not reported as a mismatch.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "seam": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/SeamId"
    }

  "type": "object"
}
```

### `dart.add`

Draw a dart on an outline edge, fold it and sew it, in one step: the edge is opened `width_mm` wide around `at_mm`, the dart's point goes `length_mm` into the piece, and its two legs are sewn together (the cloth closes when it drapes). Returns the dart's point, its two legs and the seam. Constraints on the edge are removed.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Add a dart on an edge.",
  "properties": {
    "at_mm": {
      "description": "Where the dart's middle is along the edge (mm from its start).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "edge": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
    },
    "length_mm": {
      "description": "How far into the piece its point is (mm, > 0).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "width_mm": {
      "description": "How much the dart takes in at the edge (mm, > 0).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "edge",
    "at_mm",
    "width_mm",
    "length_mm"
  ],
  "title": "DartAdd",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `pleat.add`

Fold and sew a pleat on an outline edge (a skirt's waist): from `at_mm`, a knife pleat folds `depth_mm` of cloth under (the edge's stretch of 2 × depth is sewn to itself, folded in the middle), a box pleat two such folds facing away from each other; with `stitched_mm`, the folds are also stitched down that far into the piece (along internal lines). Notches mark the fold lines. Returns the seams, then the lines and notches.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "PleatKind": {
      "description": "How a pleat folds.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "knife",
          "description": "One fold, all the same way.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "box",
          "description": "Two folds facing away from each other.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Add a pleat on an edge.",
  "properties": {
    "at_mm": {
      "description": "Where the pleat starts along the edge (mm from its start).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "depth_mm": {
      "description": "How deep each fold is (mm, > 0): a knife pleat takes up twice that\nalong the edge, a box pleat four times.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "edge": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
    },
    "kind": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PleatKind",
      "default": "knife"
    },
    "stitched_mm": {
      "description": "Stitched down this far into the piece (mm); 0 or omitted: held at\nthe edge only.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "edge",
    "at_mm",
    "depth_mm"
  ],
  "title": "PleatAdd",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.boolean`

Join two overlapping pieces into one (`union`), or cut a piece with another (`difference`: a bite out of its outline, or a hole when the other lies inside it). The result is fitted with straight and curved edges; the other piece is removed unless `keep`. Pieces that are sewn, symmetric or mirrored must be unpicked or unlinked first; notches on the changed outline go. Fails if the result would be several pieces or nothing.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "BooleanOp": {
      "description": "What a boolean keeps.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "union",
          "description": "Both pieces' cloth: one piece (they must overlap or touch).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "difference",
          "description": "The first piece without the second: a notch cut in its outline, or\na hole when the second lies inside.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Join two pieces into one, or cut one with another.",
  "properties": {
    "keep": {
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "op": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/BooleanOp"
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId",
      "description": "The piece changed."
    },
    "with": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId",
      "description": "The other piece: joined to `panel` (`union`), or cut out of it\n(`difference`). It goes, unless `keep`."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel",
    "with",
    "op"
  ],
  "title": "PanelBoolean",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `edge.lengthen`

Lengthen (mm > 0) or shorten (mm < 0) the garment at an open edge such as a hem: the edge moves along its panel's grain, and so do the edges it continues into across seams (the whole hemline), so sewn sides stay matched. Linked mirror copies follow their source.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",

      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",

  "description": "Move an open edge, and the line it continues across seams, along the\ngrain.",

    "edge": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId",
      "description": "An open (unsewn) edge: a hem, a sleeve end, a neckline."
    },
    "mm": {
      "description": "How far to move it (mm): positive makes the garment longer.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "edge",
    "mm"
  ],
  "title": "EdgeLengthen",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `edge.set_length`

Give an edge a new length (mm): it is scaled about its middle, curve included, so its end points move along it. A sewn edge's partner is scaled in the same ratio so the seam stays matched, and so are the symmetric seams of linked mirror copies (which follow their source).

```json

  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Scale an edge about its middle to a given length.",

    "edge": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
    },
    "length_mm": {
      "description": "The new length along the edge (mm).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }

### `seam.take_in`

Take in (mm > 0) or let out (mm < 0) a seam: both sides move inward by half of mm, perpendicular to the seam, so they stay matched. With `at` (an end point of the seam) only that end moves, tapering the change (e.g. take in the waist only). With linked mirror copies the symmetric seam is taken in too, so every seam stays matched.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PointId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a point, e.g. `point:1`.",
      "pattern": "^point:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "SeamId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a seam, e.g. `seam:1`.",
      "pattern": "^seam:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Take in (mm > 0) or let out (mm < 0) a seam.",
  "properties": {
    "at": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/PointId"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "An end point of the seam (on either side) to take in at that end\nonly, tapering to nothing at the other end. Omitted: the whole seam."
    },
    "mm": {
      "description": "Total width taken in (mm): each side moves half of it inward.\nNegative lets the seam out.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "seam": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/SeamId"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "seam",
    "mm"
  ],
  "title": "SeamTakeIn",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `seam.match_length`

Make the two sides of a seam the same length: the side other than `keep` is scaled about its middle to `keep`'s length (on a linked mirror copy, its source is). Afterwards `edge.set_length` keeps them equal.

  },
  "required": [
    "seam",

  "type": "object"
}
```

### `button.add`

Add a button sewn on a piece at `at` and its buttonhole on `hole_panel` (often the overlapping piece; the same piece for a cuff). `hole_at` is where the button sits once buttoned (the slit's end nearest the edge); the slit runs from there along `hole_angle_deg` for the button's diameter + 3 mm. Buttoned, the drape holds the button point and `hole_at` together. Both points must be inside their pieces. Returns the button.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{

        "null"
      ]

      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },

      "description": "Direction of the slit from `hole_at` (degrees from +X). Omitted:\nacross the piece towards its middle.",

      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "hole_at": {

### `zipper.add`

Add a zipper joining two sides (given as a seam's: a whole `edge`, consecutive `edges` or an internal `line`, maybe only `from_mm`/`to_mm` along it). Both sides start at the zipper's bottom stop: use `reversed` to walk a side from its end (b.reversed omitted: chosen as for a seam). The drape joins the sides like a seam from the bottom stop up to the slider, `open_mm` below the top (omitted: 0, closed all along). Stretches sewn or zipped already cannot be used. Returns the zipper.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "InternalLineId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a line, e.g. `line:1`.",
      "pattern": "^line:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "SeamSideSpec": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "One side of a new seam: a whole edge, a run of edges, or an internal\nline; all of it or part of it.",
      "properties": {
        "edge": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "One edge."
        },
        "edges": {
          "description": "Or consecutive outline edges of one piece, in their order around it\n(e.g. a pocket's sides and bottom).",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "from_mm": {
          "description": "Only from here along the path (mm from its start). Omitted: its\nstart.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "line": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/InternalLineId"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Or an internal line (a pocket's placement line, a tuck's line)."
        },
        "reversed": {
          "description": "Walk the side from its end instead of its start. Omitted: `false`\nfor side `a`; for side `b`, an edge sewn to its linked mirror image\nmeets it mirrored point to mirrored point (a centre seam), other\nsides are walked both the same way on the pattern (what sewing two\npanels laid side by side needs).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "to_mm": {
          "description": "Only to here (mm from the path's start). Omitted: its end.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Add a zipper between two sides.",
  "properties": {
    "a": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/SeamSideSpec",
      "description": "Its sides, as a seam's; each starts at the bottom stop."
    },
    "b": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/SeamSideSpec"
    },
    "open_mm": {
      "description": "How much of it is open from the top (mm). Omitted: closed.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "a",
    "b"
  ],
  "title": "ZipperAdd",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

          "type": "array"

          ]

Omitted: `false`\nfor side `a`; for side `b`, an edge sewn to its linked mirror image\nmeets it mirrored point to mirrored point (a centre seam), other\nsides are walked both the same way on the pattern (what sewing two\npanels laid side by side needs).",

### `elastic.shirr`

Shirr a piece: `rows` parallel rows of elastic across it, along `edge`'s chord, the first `first_mm` inside it (default 15), then every `gap_mm` (default 15), each an internal line with its elastic (`ratio`, default 0.75; `width_mm`, default 2), stopping 1 mm short of the outline. When the outline changes the rows follow it (a row the piece no longer runs across goes); `elastic.remove` on a row removes its line too. One undo step. Returns the lines and the elastics.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }

  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Shirr a piece: parallel rows of elastic.",
  "properties": {
    "edge": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId",
      "description": "The outline edge the rows run along (parallel to its chord)."
    },
    "first_mm": {
      "description": "The first row's distance from the edge (mm). Omitted: 15 mm.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "gap_mm": {
      "description": "The distance between rows (mm). Omitted: 15 mm.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    },
    "ratio": {
      "description": "Each row's elastic ratio (0.2–1). Omitted: 0.75.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "rows": {
      "description": "How many rows (1–30).",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "width_mm": {
      "description": "The elastic's width (2–50 mm). Omitted: 2 mm (shirring elastic).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel",
    "edge",
    "rows"
  ],
  "title": "ElasticShirr",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `topstitch.add`

Topstitch along a side (given as a seam's: a whole `edge`, consecutive outline `edges` or an internal `line`, maybe only `from_mm`/`to_mm` along it): `rows` (1–3, default 1), the first `offset_mm` from the side (default 6; inside the piece on outline edges, on the line's left when positive), the next `gap_mm` further (default 6), `stitch_mm` stitches (default 3), a `color` (#RRGGBB, default a darker shade of the garment's) and a `thread` (normal or heavy). Beside a seam, topstitch the edge of the piece the stitches show on. Rows are cut where they leave the piece. The cloth under them bends a little harder. Returns the topstitch (a detail).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "InternalLineId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a line, e.g. `line:1`.",
      "pattern": "^line:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "SeamSideSpec": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "One side of a new seam: a whole edge, a run of edges, or an internal\nline; all of it or part of it.",
      "properties": {
        "edge": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "One edge."
        },
        "edges": {
          "description": "Or consecutive outline edges of one piece, in their order around it\n(e.g. a pocket's sides and bottom).",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "from_mm": {
          "description": "Only from here along the path (mm from its start). Omitted: its\nstart.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "line": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/InternalLineId"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Or an internal line (a pocket's placement line, a tuck's line)."
        },
        "reversed": {
          "description": "Walk the side from its end instead of its start. Omitted: `false`\nfor side `a`; for side `b`, an edge sewn to its linked mirror image\nmeets it mirrored point to mirrored point (a centre seam), other\nsides are walked both the same way on the pattern (what sewing two\npanels laid side by side needs).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "to_mm": {
          "description": "Only to here (mm from the path's start). Omitted: its end.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "Thread": {
      "description": "The thread a topstitch is sewn with.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "normal",
          "description": "The garment's sewing thread.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "heavy",
          "description": "Topstitching thread, about twice as thick.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Add topstitching along a side.",
  "properties": {
    "color": {
      "description": "The thread's colour, `#RRGGBB`. Omitted: a darker shade of the\ngarment's.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "gap_mm": {
      "description": "The distance between rows (1–30 mm). Omitted: 6.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "offset_mm": {
      "description": "The first row's distance from the side (mm). On outline edges\n1–50, inside the piece; on an internal line −50–50, on its left\n(from its start) when positive. Omitted: 6.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "rows": {
      "description": "How many rows (1–3). Omitted: 1.",
      "format": "uint8",
      "maximum": 255,
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": [
        "integer",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "side": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/SeamSideSpec",
      "description": "Where it runs, as a seam's side (the edge of the piece the\nstitches show on)."
    },
    "stitch_mm": {
      "description": "The stitch length (1–8 mm). Omitted: 3.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "thread": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Thread"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "`normal` or `heavy` (topstitching thread). Omitted: normal."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "side"
  ],
  "title": "TopstitchAdd",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `interfacing.add`

Fuse an interfacing on a piece: on the whole piece (default), in a band `width_mm` wide (up to 300) inside consecutive outline `edges` (a collar stand, a facing, a waistband), or inside a closed internal line. Its `fabric` (woven, non_woven, knit) and `weight` (light, medium, heavy) make the cloth there heavier, thicker and much stiffer to bend and stretch. Interfacings on one piece do not overlap. It is in the tech pack's bill of materials. Returns the interfacing (a detail).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "AreaSpec": {
      "description": "Where an interfacing goes on its piece.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "The whole piece.",
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "whole",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "A band `width_mm` wide inside consecutive outline edges, in their\norder around the piece.",
          "properties": {
            "edges": {
              "items": {
                "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
              },
              "type": "array"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "band",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "width_mm": {
              "format": "double",
              "type": "number"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "edges",
            "width_mm"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "Inside a closed internal line of the piece.",
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "inside",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "line": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/InternalLineId"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "line"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    },
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "InterfacingFabric": {
      "description": "How an interfacing is made: how it stretches.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "enum": [
            "woven",
            "non_woven"
          ],
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "knit",
          "description": "Stretches across, with the cloth.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "InterfacingWeight": {
      "description": "How heavy an interfacing is.",
      "enum": [
        "light",
        "medium",
        "heavy"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "InternalLineId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a line, e.g. `line:1`.",
      "pattern": "^line:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Fuse an interfacing on a piece.",
  "properties": {
    "area": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/AreaSpec"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Where: `{\"kind\": \"whole\"}`, `{\"kind\": \"band\", \"edges\": [...],\n\"width_mm\": 30}` or `{\"kind\": \"inside\", \"line\": \"line:7\"}`.\nOmitted: the whole piece."
    },
    "fabric": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/InterfacingFabric"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],

    "panel": {

    "weight": {

        {

        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "`light`, `medium` or `heavy`. Omitted: medium."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel"
  ],
  "title": "InterfacingAdd",
  "type": "object"
}

### `quilting.add`

Quilt a piece (or the inside of a closed internal `line` on it) over a padding: `pattern` channels or diamonds (default), `angle_deg` from the grainline (default 45 for diamonds, 0 for channels), lines `spacing_mm` apart (default 50), a padding `loft_mm` thick (default 8) weighing `padding_gsm` (default 100), `stitch_mm` stitches and a thread `color`. The cloth there drapes as shell, padding and lining together, folds along the stitched lines, and puffs out between them in the views. One quilting per area. Returns the quilting (a detail).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "InternalLineId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a line, e.g. `line:1`.",
      "pattern": "^line:[1-9][0-9]*$",

    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "QuiltPattern": {
      "description": "How a quilting's lines run.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "channels",
          "description": "Parallel lines.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "diamonds",
          "description": "Two families of lines, at the angle each side of the grainline.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Quilt a piece, or the inside of a closed line on it.",
  "properties": {
    "angle_deg": {
      "description": "The lines' angle from the grainline (degrees; each side of it for\ndiamonds). Omitted: 45 for diamonds, 0 for channels.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "color": {
      "description": "The thread's colour, `#RRGGBB`. Omitted: a darker shade of the\ngarment's.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]

    "line": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/InternalLineId"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Only inside this closed internal line. Omitted: the whole piece."
    },
    "loft_mm": {
      "description": "The padding's thickness (1–30 mm). Omitted: 8.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "padding_gsm": {
      "description": "The padding's weight (10–600 g/m²). Omitted: 100.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    },
    "pattern": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/QuiltPattern"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "`channels` (parallel lines) or `diamonds`. Omitted: diamonds."
    },
    "spacing_mm": {
      "description": "The distance between parallel lines (15–150 mm). Omitted: 50.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "stitch_mm": {
      "description": "The stitches' length (1–8 mm). Omitted: 3.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel"
  ],
  "title": "QuiltingAdd",
  "type": "object"
}

### `garment.set_fabric_details`

Set the garment's fabric as bought: its weight (g/m², also the cloth's mass in the drape), the width it is sold in (mm) and its price per metre. Sets all three: an omitted one goes back to its default (the fabric's usual weight, no width, no price). Used by production.indicators and marker.compute.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "GarmentId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a garment, e.g. `garment:1`.",
      "pattern": "^garment:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Set the garment's fabric as bought: weight, width, price.",
  "properties": {
    "garment": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/GarmentId"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Defaults to the project's garment."
    },
    "price_per_m": {
      "description": "Price of one metre of length (any currency, ≥ 0); omitted: none.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "weight_gsm": {
      "description": "Weight (g/m², 10–2000); omitted: the fabric's usual weight.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "width_mm": {
      "description": "Width the fabric is sold in (mm, 100–5000); omitted: none (a\nmarker then takes 1500 mm).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "GarmentSetFabricDetails",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

{
  "$defs": {

        {

### `garment.set_print`

Put a print on the garment's fabric: a built-in one (stripes, gingham, dots, twill, drawn in the garment's colour) or a PNG/JPEG image in the project folder (`r3d texture` copies one in). The print lies along each piece's grainline at its real size (`width_mm` × `height_mm` per repeat), turned by `angle_deg`; it shows in the 3D view, photos, the board and the glTF/OBJ exports. Replaces the previous print.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "BuiltinPrint": {
      "description": "The prints the app ships, drawn by [`builtin`].",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "stripes",
          "description": "A stripe of the colour and one of the ground, along the grain.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "gingham",
          "description": "Crossing bands of the colour, darker where they cross.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "dots",
          "description": "Dots of the colour on the ground, in staggered rows (two per\nrepeat).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "twill",
          "description": "A 2/1 twill weave: diagonal ribs of the colour and a lighter\nthread.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "GarmentId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a garment, e.g. `garment:1`.",
      "pattern": "^garment:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "PrintSource": {
      "description": "Where a print's pixels come from.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "One of the prints the app ships, in the garment's colour.",
          "properties": {
            "builtin": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/BuiltinPrint"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "builtin"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "A PNG or JPEG file, relative to the project folder.",
          "properties": {
            "image": {
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "image"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Put a print on the garment's fabric.",
  "properties": {
    "angle_deg": {
      "default": 0.0,
      "description": "The print turned from the grainline (degrees, counter-clockwise);\n0: the image's top along the grain.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "garment": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/GarmentId"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Defaults to the project's garment."
    },
    "height_mm": {
      "description": "Height of one repeat along the grain (mm, 1–5000); omitted: the\nimage's proportions (square for built-ins).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "print": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PrintSource",
      "description": "`{\"builtin\": \"stripes\" | \"gingham\" | \"dots\" | \"twill\"}`, or\n`{\"image\": \"textures/name.png\"}`: a PNG or JPEG file in the project\nfolder (relative, forward slashes)."
    },
    "width_mm": {
      "description": "Width of one repeat across the grain (mm, 1–5000); omitted: the\nbuilt-in's usual repeat (20 mm stripes, 12 mm gingham, 16 mm dots,\n4 mm twill), 100 mm for an image.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "print"
  ],
  "title": "GarmentSetPrint",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

Shift (mm) and turn (degrees) the garment's print on one piece, e.g. to centre a motif on a front or match stripes across a seam. Zero for both lays the print as on every other piece.

{
  "$defs": {

### `photo.set_scene`

Set how the project's photos are taken: the light (a studio, or an environment by built-in name or `.hdr` path in the project), its turn and brightness, an environment's size (its radius around the model: the floor ends there and the rest of the picture stands around it), the camera (the point it looks at, its turn, height angle, distance and focal length) and the image size. The app's photo scene saves it; `render_photo` and `r3d render --view photo` use it unless their arguments say otherwise. `null` forgets it.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PhotoCamera": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "Where the photo's camera stands: it turns around the point it looks\nat. Metres in the simulation are millimetres here (Y up).",
      "properties": {
        "distance_mm": {
          "description": "Distance from the point looked at (mm, 300–20 000).",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "focal_mm": {
          "description": "Focal length on a 24 × 36 mm frame (mm, 10–300): its 24 mm side\nlies along the image's shorter side.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "pitch_deg": {
          "description": "Height angle (degrees, −80 to 80; positive: from above).",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "target_mm": {
          "description": "The point looked at (mm).",
          "items": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "maxItems": 3,
          "minItems": 3,
          "type": "array"
        },
        "yaw_deg": {
          "description": "Turn around the vertical (degrees; 0: from the front, 90: from the\nbody's left side).",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "target_mm",
        "yaw_deg",
        "pitch_deg",
        "distance_mm",
        "focal_mm"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "PhotoLight": {
      "description": "What lights a photo.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "A key, a fill and a rim light on a light grey backdrop.",
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "studio",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "Large soft boxes on a white backdrop, few shadows.",
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "soft",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "One hard key and a rim on a dark backdrop.",
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "dramatic",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "A picture of the light all around: a built-in environment's name\n(`ferndale`, `neon`, `pav`, `kontrast`, `wooden`) or a `.hdr` file\nin the project folder (relative, forward slashes).",
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "environment",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "name": {
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "name"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    },
    "PhotoSetup": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "How the project's photos are taken.",
      "properties": {
        "brightness": {
          "default": 1.0,
          "description": "Factor on the light (0.05–20; 1: the usual exposure).",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "camera": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/PhotoCamera"
        },
        "light": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/PhotoLight"
        },
        "place_size_m": {
          "default": 3.0,
          "description": "How far an environment's walls stand from the model at floor\nlevel (m, 1–100; 3: a room): its floor ends there and the rest of\nits picture stands around it.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "size": {
          "description": "Image size in pixels (16–4096 a side); omitted: the 3D view's size\nin the app, the command's own elsewhere.",
          "items": {
            "format": "uint32",
            "minimum": 0,
            "type": "integer"
          },
          "maxItems": 2,
          "minItems": 2,
          "type": [
            "array",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "turn_deg": {
          "default": 0.0,
          "description": "Turn of the light around the model (degrees, counter-clockwise\nseen from above); at 0 an environment's centre is behind the model\nand the studio's key light on the camera's left.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "light",
        "camera"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Set how the project's photos are taken, or forget it.",
  "properties": {
    "scene": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/PhotoSetup"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The light, its turn and brightness, the camera and the image size;\n`null` forgets them (photos go back to their defaults)."
    }
  },
  "title": "PhotoSetScene",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `garment.arrange`

Place every panel around the body for the simulation, side by side in the order the seams join them (a panel's right side continues into the next panel; each takes a share of the turn in proportion to its width), tops at the avatar's waist (its narrowest girth) unless top_cm is given. Panels placed on an arm (sleeves) or flat keep their placement. Re-run it after adding panels or seams.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Place every panel around the body.",
  "properties": {
    "top_cm": {
      "description": "Height of the panels' tops (cm). Default: the avatar's waist.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "GarmentArrange",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `garment.set_layer`

Choose where a garment is worn among the others: layer 0 is next to the body, the others move to make room. The garment worn over another drapes over it: a shirt under trousers is tucked in, over them it is worn out.

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "GarmentId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a garment, e.g. `garment:1`.",

      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",

  "description": "Choose where a garment is worn among the others.",

    "garment": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/GarmentId"
    },

      "description": "0 next to the body; the garments from there on move up or down to\nmake room. A shirt tucked into trousers is under them (a lower\nlayer), a shirt worn out over them.",

      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [

    "layer"
  ],

  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>
