### `grading.set_sizes`

Set the project's size range: the sizes from smallest to largest, each with how its body differs from the base size's (the avatar; cm), and the base size the pattern is drawn in. Garments drafted from a template and not graded yet are graded by drafting the template for every size's body. Points keep their grade in the sizes that stay (by name); new sizes are inter- or extrapolated. Changing the base redraws the pattern in that size. See grading.use_chart for standard sizes.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "SizeSpec": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "One size of a range, as commands take it.",
      "properties": {
        "age_years": {
          "default": 0.0,
          "description": "How many years older the size's body is (children's ranges;\ndefault 0).",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "bust_cm": {
          "default": 0.0,
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "height_cm": {
          "default": 0.0,
          "description": "How the size's body differs from the base size's (cm; default 0).",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "hips_cm": {
          "default": 0.0,
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "name": {
          "description": "As on the label: \"38\", \"M\".",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "waist_cm": {
          "default": 0.0,
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "name"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Set the project's size range.",
  "properties": {
    "base": {
      "description": "The size the pattern is drawn in (a name from `sizes`).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "sizes": {
      "description": "From the smallest to the largest; at least two, names unique.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/SizeSpec"
      },
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "sizes",
    "base"
  ],
  "title": "GradingSetSizes",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `grading.use_chart`

Set the project's size range from a built-in European chart (`women` 32–56, `men` 44–60, every second size; `girls` and `boys` by age 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14; `babies` 3m, 6m, 12m, 18m, 24m): the sizes from `from` to `to`, drawn in `base`. Each size's body differs from the avatar as the chart's sizes differ from its base size; without an avatar, the chart's base body becomes the avatar. Garments drafted from a template, before or after, are graded to every size; grade other points with point.set_grade.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "SizeChart": {
      "description": "A built-in size chart.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "women",
          "description": "European women's sizes 32 to 56 (bust 76–134 cm).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "men",
          "description": "European men's sizes 44 to 60 (chest 88–120 cm).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "girls",
          "description": "Girls' sizes by age, 2 to 14 years (height 92–164 cm).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "boys",
          "description": "Boys' sizes by age, 2 to 14 years (height 92–164 cm).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "babies",
          "description": "Babies' sizes by age in months, 3m to 24m (height 62–88 cm).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Set the size range from a built-in chart.",
  "properties": {
    "base": {
      "description": "The size the pattern is drawn in, e.g. \"40\".",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "chart": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/SizeChart",
      "description": "`women` (32–56), `men` (44–60), `girls` or `boys` (ages 2–14) or\n`babies` (3m–24m)."
    },
    "from": {
      "description": "Smallest size of the range, e.g. \"36\".",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "to": {
      "description": "Largest size, e.g. \"52\".",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "chart",
    "from",
    "to",
    "base"
  ],
  "title": "GradingUseChart",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

Remove the size range and every point's grade: the pattern stays in its base size. Destructive: requires "confirm": true.

### `point.set_grade`

Set how a contour point moves from size to size (its grade rule): either `step`, the same move from each size to the next (mm, [x, y]; e.g. [5, 0] moves the point 5 mm outward per size), or `offsets`, where it is in some sizes relative to the base size, the others inter- or extrapolated. A zero step removes the rule. Curve handles, internal lines and pins follow the points; linked mirror copies follow their source, mirrored.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PointId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a point, e.g. `point:1`.",
      "pattern": "^point:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Set a point's grade rule.",
  "properties": {
    "offsets": {
      "additionalProperties": {
        "items": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "maxItems": 2,
        "minItems": 2,
        "type": "array"
      },
      "description": "Or where the point is in some sizes, from its base position (mm,\nby size name); the other sizes are inter- or extrapolated.",
      "type": [
        "object",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "point": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PointId"
    },
    "step": {
      "description": "The same move from each size to the next (mm, [x, y]).",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "point"
  ],
  "title": "PointSetGrade",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `template.apply`

Draft a starter garment (t_shirt, shirt, trousers, hoodie, joggers, jeans, shorts, dress, straight_skirt, a_line_skirt, tote_bag, sweatshirt, and for babies and children bodysuit, pyjama_top, pyjama_bottoms, and the sets pyjama and jogging_suit (joggers and a sweatshirt), which add their bottoms and then their top worn over them as two garments, the given length and ease being the top's; library.list gives their kinds) from sizes in cm, the avatar's measurements filling in any left out: its pieces are drawn, sewn, placed around the body and given a fabric, ready to simulate and edit. In a project without panels its garment takes the template's name (the project keeps its own); in a project with pieces the template becomes a garment of its own, worn over the others (see garment.set_layer). ### `pattern.import`

Add pattern pieces in one step: for each, its sewing line (as in panel.create_path), seam allowance, grainline angle, notches (points near the outline) and internal lines. Placed to the right of the existing pieces unless keep_position. `import.pattern` reads them from a DXF, SVG or PDF file. Returns, for each piece, its panel, points and edges, then its notches and lines.

```json
{
  "$defs": {

        "segments"
```

### `pattern.import_parametric`

Import a Seamly2D or Valentina pattern (the text of a .sm2d or .val file, and of its measurement file if it has one): its drafting steps are run with the measurements (without a measurement file, the avatar's height, bust, waist and hips) and its pieces added, with seam allowances, notches, grainlines and internal paths, laid out side by side to the right of the board. They make a garment of their own (the project's only garment on an empty board), which keeps the pattern: graded in every size of a size range, and drafted again for another body with garment.redraft. `import.pattern` reads the files. Returns the garment if one was added, then the panels.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Import a parametric pattern as a garment of its own.",
  "properties": {
    "file": {
      "description": "The pattern file's name, as shown (`imports/skirt.val`).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "measurements": {
      "description": "The text of its measurement file (`.vit`, `.vst`, `.smis`,\n`.smms`), if it has one. Without it, the pattern is drafted for the\navatar's height, bust, waist and hips.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "pattern": {
      "description": "The pattern file's text: a Seamly2D (`.sm2d`) or Valentina\n(`.val`) pattern.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "file",
    "pattern"
  ],
  "title": "PatternImportParametric",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `garment.redraft`

Draft a garment imported from a Seamly2D or Valentina pattern again for a body (default: the avatar's): its pattern is run with that body's height, bust, waist and hips in place of the measurement file's (a multisize file is read at the size that fits it), and each point and curve moves as the pattern moves it, so changes made to the pieces since are kept; internal lines and pins follow. A piece whose outline gained or lost points is left as it is and listed in `skipped`. In a size range the garment is graded again.

```json
          "type": "number"

          "type": "number"

          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "masculinity": {
          "description": "0 = feminine body, 1 = masculine body.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "waist_cm": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "masculinity",
        "height_cm",
        "bust_cm",
        "waist_cm",
        "hips_cm"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "GarmentId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a garment, e.g. `garment:1`.",
      "pattern": "^garment:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Draft an imported parametric pattern again for a body.",
  "properties": {
    "body": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Body"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],

    "garment": {
```

### `pattern.add`

Add the garments of a saved pattern (a project document, as library patterns are kept; library.add reads one from the library) to this project: each one with its pieces, seams, notches, internal lines, pins, construction details, buttons, zippers, constraints and variables (a variable the project already has keeps the project's formula), its fabric, colour, print and notes, worn over the garments already there. Pieces drafted from the body are drafted again for this project's avatar, keeping what was done to them since: from a template (the template's body measurements follow the body; lengths and ease stay), from a Seamly2D/Valentina pattern, and dimensions given by formulas; the others come as drawn. In a size range they are graded. Returns the garments, then the panels and seams.

```json
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Add the garments of a saved pattern.",

    "pattern": {
      "description": "A Rustle3D project document (`{\"format\": \"rustle3d.project\",\n\"schema_version\": N, \"project\": {...}}`, as `project.json` holds\nit), of this version of the app or an older one."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "pattern"
  ],
  "title": "PatternAdd",
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `avatar.use_measurements`

Take the avatar's measurements from a Seamly2D or Valentina measurement file (its text): height, bust, waist and hips (height, bust_circ, waist_circ, hip_circ) become the body, the file's gender its masculinity; its other measurements become variables for formulas (in mm; a custom @name without the @). A multisize file also sets the size range: its sizes along the chest (or its first) dimension, its base size as the base. `import.measurements` reads the file.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json

  "properties": {
    "measurements": {
      "description": "The text of a Seamly2D or Valentina measurement file: individual\n(`.vit`, `.smis`) or multisize (`.vst`, `.smms`).",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "measurements"
  ],
  "title": "AvatarUseMeasurements",
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `constraint.add`

Add a constraint (fixed, coincident, horizontal, vertical, parallel, perpendicular, tangent, equal_length, on_edge) or a dimension (distance, length, angle) on contour points and edges. A dimension with a `formula` (e.g. "waist / 4 + 10 mm") takes its value from the body's measurements and the variables, now and whenever they change, and in every size of the range. The drawing is solved at once: the geometry moves as little as possible so that every constraint holds; constraints that cannot all hold are refused (`constraints_unsolvable`). With `measure`, a dimension keeps the value it has now. Returns the constraint; `constraint.list` shows them with the freedom left.

### `point.set_smooth`

Make a contour point smooth (no corner: its two edges become curves whose handles line up, and stay so through a `tangent` constraint) or a corner again (the constraint is removed, the shape stays).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PointId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a point, e.g. `point:1`.",
      "pattern": "^point:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Make a point smooth or a corner.",
  "properties": {
    "point": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PointId"
    },
    "smooth": {
      "description": "`true`: the outline passes through the point without a corner (its\ntwo edges become curves with aligned handles, kept aligned by a\n`tangent` constraint); `false`: a corner again (the constraint goes,\nthe shape stays).",
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "point",
    "smooth"
  ],
  "title": "PointSetSmooth",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.unfold`

Make a half piece whole and symmetric: it is unfolded across one of its straight edges (the axis, e.g. a centre front), which disappears. The other half follows every later change of the drawn half (points, curves, notches) and cannot be edited itself; seams and notches can go on it. panel.unlink makes the halves independent. Returns the new points and edges of the reflected half.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Unfold a half piece on one of its edges.",
  "properties": {
    "edge": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId",
      "description": "A straight edge of the piece: the axis (a centre front on the fold)."
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel",
    "edge"
  ],
  "title": "PanelUnfold",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

```json
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": "array"
```

```json
      "type": [
```

### `panel.create_sector`

Create an arc sector, the piece of a circle skirt: the inner arc is `inner_length_mm` long (the waist it covers), the outer arc `length_mm` further out (the hem), over `sweep_deg` (e.g. 180 for half a circle skirt). The radius comes from the waist: inner_length / sweep. The piece hangs below `centre`, its waist on top. Returns the panel, then its points (the hem from left to right, then the waist from right to left), then its edges.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Create an arc sector: a ring cut between two radii.",
  "properties": {
    "centre": {
      "default": [
        0.0,
        0.0
      ],
      "description": "Centre of the circles on the board (mm). Defaults to `[0, 0]`; the\npiece hangs below it.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "grain_angle_deg": {
      "default": 90.0,
      "description": "Grainline angle in degrees from +X. Defaults to 90 (vertical).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "inner_length_mm": {
      "description": "Length of the inner arc (mm, > 0): the waist this piece covers.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "length_mm": {
      "description": "Distance from the inner to the outer arc (mm, > 0): the skirt's\nlength.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "Panel name. Defaults to \"Panel N\".",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "sweep_deg": {
      "description": "The angle the piece covers (degrees, more than 0 and less than\n360): 180 for a half circle, 90 for a quarter. A full circle skirt\nis two half circles, or four quarters, sewn together.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "inner_length_mm",
    "length_mm",
    "sweep_deg"
  ],
  "title": "PanelCreateSector",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `edge.set_arc`

Make an edge a circular arc through its two ends, bulging `bulge_mm` from the straight line (positive outward). An arc over 90° is split into edges of at most 90° (new points between them); then the constraints on the edge are removed and its notches spread along the arc. Returns the new points and edges, if any.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Turn an edge into a circular arc.",
  "properties": {
    "bulge_mm": {
      "description": "How far the arc's middle is from the straight line between the\nedge's ends (mm, not 0): positive bulges outward (to the right of\nthe edge, as outlines turn counter-clockwise), negative inward.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "edge": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "edge",
    "bulge_mm"
  ],
  "title": "EdgeSetArc",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `constraint.set_formula`

Give a dimension a formula of the body's measurements and the variables (e.g. "waist / 4 + 10 mm"): its value follows them, the drawing is redrawn when the body changes, and each size of the range is drafted with its own measurements (the points the formulas move are graded by them). Without `formula`, the dimension keeps its value. Errors say what is wrong: formula.syntax, formula.unknown_name, formula.cycle, formula.unit, formula.no_body, formula.domain, formula.range.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "ConstraintId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a constraint, e.g. `constraint:1`.",
      "pattern": "^constraint:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Give a dimension a formula, or take it away.",
  "properties": {
    "constraint": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/ConstraintId"
    },
    "formula": {
      "description": "E.g. \"waist / 4 + 10 mm\", \"bust / 2 + ease\": arithmetic (+ - * /,\nparentheses, min, max, abs, sqrt) on numbers with units (mm, cm, m,\nin, deg), the body's measurements (height, bust, waist, hips) and\nvariables. A length for a distance or a length, a plain number\n(degrees) for an angle. Omitted: the dimension keeps its value and\nno longer follows the body.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "constraint"
  ],
  "title": "ConstraintSetFormula",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `constraint.rename`

Name a dimension (e.g. "armhole"): formulas can then use it like a variable (its formula when it has one, else its value), e.g. a sleeve cap's length "armhole + 1.5 cm". Renaming rewrites the formulas that use the old name; taking the name away is refused while a formula uses it (formula.unknown_name).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "ConstraintId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a constraint, e.g. `constraint:1`.",
      "pattern": "^constraint:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Name a dimension, so that formulas can use it, or take its name away.",
  "properties": {
    "constraint": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/ConstraintId"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "As a variable's: a letter or _, then letters, digits or _ (not a\nbody measurement, a function, a unit, a variable or another\ndimension's name). Omitted: no name.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "constraint"
  ],
  "title": "ConstraintRename",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `constraint.place_label`

Move a dimension's label (only the label: the drawing stays as it is), as an offset in mm from where it is drawn by default; without `offset`, back there.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "ConstraintId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a constraint, e.g. `constraint:1`.",
      "pattern": "^constraint:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Place a dimension's label by hand.",
  "properties": {
    "constraint": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/ConstraintId"
    },
    "offset": {
      "description": "mm from where the label is drawn by default (the middle of the\ndimension line, of the edge, of the angle). Omitted: back there.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "constraint"
  ],
  "title": "ConstraintPlaceLabel",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `variable.set`

Set a named variable that formulas can use (e.g. ease = "2 cm", dart = "(hips - waist) / 8"): created, or changed, and every formula using it follows.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Set a named variable for formulas.",
  "properties": {
    "formula": {
      "description": "Its formula, e.g. \"2 cm\" or \"bust / 20 + 5 mm\".",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "A letter or _, then letters, digits or _ (not a body measurement,\na function or a unit).",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "name",
    "formula"
  ],
  "title": "VariableSet",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

```json
}
```

## Queries

Read-only. Lengths in mm, areas in mm², rounded to 0.001.

### `project.summary`

Project name, display unit, the garments (fabric, colour, notes, print), the size range (names, base, shown; null without one), `object` (its stuffing when the project makes an object, null for a garment worn; spec 36), entity counts and a summary of every panel.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Project name, units, counts and a summary of every panel.",
  "title": "ProjectSummary",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

List panels with area, perimeter, bounding box and validity.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "List panels with area, perimeter and bounding box.",
  "title": "PanelList",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.get`

Full geometry of a panel: its edges in contour order with point IDs, positions, curve and length; graded points have their `grade`, their offset in each size of the range (grading.get's order). With `size`, the geometry in that size.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Full geometry of one panel.",
  "properties": {
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    },
    "size": {
      "description": "A size of the project's range: the geometry in that size. Default:\nas drawn (the base size).",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel"
  ],
  "title": "PanelGet",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.copy`

Copy pieces into a clip (JSON) for panel.paste, in this project or another one: the pieces with their points, curves, notches, internal lines, pins, grade rules, construction details (elastics, topstitching, interfacing, quilting), buttons and zippers, the seams between them, their constraints with the construction lines these use, and the mirror links among them. Seams, trims and links to pieces left out are not copied.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Copy pieces: a clip to give to panel.paste.",
  "properties": {
    "panels": {
      "description": "The pieces to copy (at least one).",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
      },
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panels"
  ],
  "title": "PanelCopy",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `avatar.get`

The avatar's requested measurements, its preset, the measurements the fitted 3D body actually reaches (they can differ slightly for extreme sizes), and the heights above the floor (cm) of its waist (narrowest girth), hips (largest girth) and crotch, to draft and place skirts and trousers (panel.place top_cm). `measures`: every other measurement (neck, shoulder_width, arm_length…, as formulas name them) with its group (torso, arms, legs), its value in cm, whether it is `estimated` from the four (else typed with avatar.set_measures), whether the 3D body `follows` it, and what the built-in body `reached_cm` (null on an imported body). Null when there is no avatar.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The avatar and what the fitted body actually measures.",
  "title": "AvatarGet",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `avatar.presets`

Built-in body presets: standard women's and men's sizes, as {name, body} pairs usable with avatar.set.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The built-in body presets (standard sizes).",
  "title": "AvatarPresets",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `avatar.size_body`

The body (for avatar.set) of a size of a built-in chart, shaped by a `silhouette` that keeps its bust and moves its waist and hips: `balanced` (as the chart), `hourglass`, `pear`, `straight`, `round`, `inverted_triangle`, or for children `slim`, `balanced`, `round` (grading.charts lists each chart's); `height_cm` to change its height.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "Silhouette": {
      "description": "A body's shape at a size: where its waist and hips stand from the\nchart's, which keeps the bust (or the chest). Approximate values from\ngeneral garment-making knowledge.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "balanced",
          "description": "As the chart (a woman's waist 18 cm under the bust, hips 8 over;\na man's waist 12 under the chest, hips 4 over).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "hourglass",
          "description": "A marked waist, the hips as the chart (X).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "pear",
          "description": "Hips fuller than the chart (A).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "straight",
          "description": "Little waist: waist fuller, hips narrower (H).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "round",
          "description": "Fuller at the waist (O).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "inverted_triangle",
          "description": "Narrower hips under a broad chest (V).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "slim",
          "description": "Slimmer all round (a child's chart; an adult's waist and hips).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "SizeChart": {
      "description": "A built-in size chart.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "women",
          "description": "European women's sizes 32 to 56 (bust 76–134 cm).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "men",
          "description": "European men's sizes 44 to 60 (chest 88–120 cm).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "girls",
          "description": "Girls' sizes by age, 2 to 14 years (height 92–164 cm).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "boys",
          "description": "Boys' sizes by age, 2 to 14 years (height 92–164 cm).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "babies",
          "description": "Babies' sizes by age in months, 3m to 24m (height 62–88 cm).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The body of a size of a built-in chart.",
  "properties": {
    "chart": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/SizeChart",
      "description": "`women`, `men`, `girls`, `boys` or `babies`."
    },
    "height_cm": {
      "description": "Its height (cm); default the chart's.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "silhouette": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Silhouette",
      "default": "balanced",
      "description": "Its shape (default `balanced`, as the chart)."
    },
    "size": {
      "description": "A size of the chart, e.g. \"38\" (grading.charts lists them).",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "chart",
    "size"
  ],
  "title": "AvatarSizeBody",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `avatar.check`

Check the imported body before draping: `ready` (no error), triangle and vertex counts, height, units/up axis/turn used, whether the file has a skeleton, `items` (each a stable `code`, a `severity` error/warning/info and `args`: file.unavailable, mesh.open, mesh.non_manifold, mesh.pieces, mesh.heavy, mesh.coarse, mesh.reoriented, mesh.inside_out, mesh.degenerate, scale.height, orientation.up, orientation.facing, points.outside, points.side, measurements.clamped, motion.rig with `source` file or points: what places the skeleton the body moves with) and the arrangement points with their distance to the surface (mm, negative inside). Fails when the avatar has no imported body.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The check of the imported body (spec 27).",
  "title": "AvatarCheck",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

List the constraints and dimensions (on one piece, or all): each with its piece, its kind and what it names, a dimension's value and what the drawing measures now, whether it holds, and `marks` (where its points and the middles of its edges are, mm). `groups` are constraints sharing points, each with `freedom` (ways the constrained geometry can still move, moving or turning a piece as a whole included) and `redundant` constraints (over-constrained: they repeat what others say).

```json
        {
          "type": "null"
```

### `production.indicators`

Production indicators, per garment (next to the body first): the weight in use (g/m²) and the fabric details as set (weight_gsm, width_mm, price_per_m), each piece's area (sewing line, holes left out, mm²), cut area (with its seam allowance), perimeter (mm) and mass (cut area × weight, g), and the garment's totals. In one size of the range with `size`.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Area, cut area, mass of each piece and totals per garment.",
  "properties": {
    "size": {
      "description": "A size of the range, by name; omitted: the pattern as drawn (the\nbase size).",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ProductionIndicators",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `marker.compute`

Lay the pieces of a garment, in one or several sizes, out on a strip of fabric (a marker; raster bottom-left-fill, deterministic): each piece by its cutting line, its grainline along the fabric's length (0° or 180°; every 45° with free_grain), once per size unless `quantities` says otherwise. Returns the length (mm), efficiency (% of the fabric used), yardage (m), cost (from the garment's price per metre) and where each piece lies. Fails with marker_too_narrow when a piece is wider than the fabric.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "GarmentId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a garment, e.g. `garment:1`.",
      "pattern": "^garment:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "MarkerSpec": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "What to lay out, and on what.",
      "properties": {
        "garment": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/GarmentId"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "The garment whose pieces are laid out; omitted: the project's only\ngarment (required when there are several)."
        },
        "quantities": {
          "description": "Pieces cut another number of times than once, turned over in\npairs, or with a free grain.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/PieceQuantity"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "sizes": {
          "description": "Sizes of the range to cut, by name (each piece once per size);\nomitted: the pattern as drawn (the base size).",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": [
            "array",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "step_mm": {
          "description": "Raster cell of the nesting (mm, 2–20, default 5): smaller is\ntighter and slower.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "width_mm": {
          "description": "Usable fabric width (mm, 300–3000); omitted: the garment's fabric\nwidth, else 1500.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "PieceQuantity": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "How many times a piece is cut in a marker, and how.",
      "properties": {
        "count": {
          "default": 1,
          "description": "Copies per size (0–50; 0 leaves the piece out). Default 1.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "free_grain": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "The piece has no grain to follow (felt, interfacing, a bias\npiece): it may lie at every 45°.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "pairs": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Every second copy is turned over (a left and a right).",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "panel": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "panel"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Lay out the pieces of a garment on the fabric (a marker).",
  "properties": {
    "marker": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/MarkerSpec",
      "default": {},
      "description": "What to lay out, and on what."
    },
    "outlines": {
      "default": false,
      "description": "Include each piece's outlines (cutting and sewing lines, holes, in\nmarker mm) in the result.",
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  },
  "title": "MarkerCompute",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

## Actions

Operations that write files (not undoable). Paths are relative to the project folder and cannot leave it.

### `export.svg`

Export all panels as an SVG at 1:1 scale (cutting and sewing lines, notches, internal lines, grainlines, labels, 100 mm test square). With `sizes`, the pattern in those sizes of the range: one alone, or a graded nest (the base size in full, the others' cutting lines in colour with a legend). Returns the written path, relative to the project folder.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Export the pattern as SVG at 1:1 scale.",
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "description": "Output path relative to the project folder. Defaults to\n`exports/<project name>.svg`.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "sizes": {
      "description": "Sizes of the range to export, by name: one size alone, or several\nnested (a graded nest). Default: the pattern as drawn (base size).",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ExportSvg",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `simulate`

Drape the placed and sewn panels on the avatar for a number of frames (1/60 s each, deterministic) and cache the result in the project, so `r3d render --view 3d` shows it. With `motion`, the avatar walks, turns or raises its arms after 1.5 s and the cloth follows (or, with `motion_file`, plays a motion captured on a person from a BVH file in the project folder); renders and exports then show the body and the garment as they are at the last frame. Returns the garment's extent, how open the seams are, how many points buttons and closed zippers hold and how far apart they still are, each elastic's length on the cloth against its relaxed length, and whether the cloth has settled.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "AvatarMotion": {
      "description": "A motion of the avatar.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "walk",
          "description": "Walking on the spot (a 1 s step cycle).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "turn",
          "description": "Half a turn to the left and back (6 s).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "raise_arms",
          "description": "Both arms raised overhead and lowered (4 s).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "idle",
          "description": "Standing at rest: the weight shifting from leg to leg, breathing\n(8 s).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Drape the garment headless and cache the result.",
  "properties": {
    "frames": {
      "default": 300,
      "description": "Frames of 1/60 s to simulate (1–3600, default 300 = 5 s).",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "motion": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/AvatarMotion"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "A motion of the avatar, started after 1.5 s of draping (once the\ngarment has closed); the cloth follows it. Omitted: the avatar\nstands still."
    },
    "motion_file": {
      "description": "Instead of `motion`: a BVH file of a motion captured on a person,\nrelative to the project folder, retargeted to the avatar and\nplayed in a loop on the spot.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "Simulate",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `export.pdf`

Export all panels as a PDF at 1:1 scale, tiled on A4/Letter pages (labelled A1, A2…, with overlap guides) or on one large page. Print at 100 % and check the 100 mm test square. With `sizes`, the pattern in those sizes of the range: one alone, or a graded nest. Returns the written path and page count.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PaperSpec": {
      "description": "Page layout of a PDF export.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "a4",
          "description": "A4 tiles to print at home.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "letter",
          "description": "US Letter tiles to print at home.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "single",
          "description": "One page as large as the pattern (plotter, print shop).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Export the pattern as a PDF at 1:1 scale.",
  "properties": {
    "paper": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PaperSpec",
      "default": "a4",
      "description": "`a4` (default) or `letter` tiles with overlap and assembly guides,\nor `single` for one large page."
    },
    "path": {
      "description": "Output path relative to the project folder. Defaults to\n`exports/<project name>.pdf`.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "sizes": {
      "description": "Sizes of the range to export, by name: one size alone, or several\nnested (a graded nest). Default: the pattern as drawn (base size).",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ExportPdf",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `export.gltf`

Export the draped garment as glTF 2.0 binary (GLB): one named node and mesh per piece, metres, Y up, texture coordinates from the pattern along each piece's grainline (in repeats of the garment's print, embedded as its base colour texture; 1 unit = 1 m of fabric without one), the fabric as a PBR material with KHR_materials_sheen; the avatar too if asked. Uses the cached drape from `simulate` if it is up to date, otherwise the starting positions, and says which. Returns the written path.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Export the draped garment as glTF 2.0 (GLB).",
  "properties": {
    "avatar": {
      "default": false,
      "description": "Include the avatar as its own node (default false).",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "path": {
      "description": "Output path relative to the project folder. Defaults to\n`exports/<project name>.glb`.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ExportGltf",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `export.obj`

Export the draped garment as Wavefront OBJ: one object per piece, metres, Y up, texture coordinates from the pattern along each piece's grainline, smooth normals; with an MTL file beside it (one material per garment, its colour, and its print's image as `map_Kd`, written beside it too). Uses the cached drape from `simulate` if it is up to date, otherwise the starting positions, and says which. Returns the written path.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Export the draped garment as Wavefront OBJ.",
  "properties": {
    "avatar": {
      "default": false,
      "description": "Include the avatar as its own object (default false).",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "path": {
      "description": "Output path relative to the project folder. Defaults to\n`exports/<project name>.obj`.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ExportObj",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `export.game`

Export the draped garment ready for a game engine as glTF 2.0 binary (GLB): per garment one mesh per level of detail (`lods`, ratios of the triangle count; simplified by quadric error metrics, the pieces' edges kept), texture coordinates in an atlas of the pieces, the full drape's wrinkles baked into a tangent-space normal map for each lower LOD (`normal_map` pixels), tangents, the print baked into a base-colour atlas, `sides` double_sided or a `shell` of `thickness_mm`, and with `skin` the avatar's 24-bone skeleton in the pose the body stands in (an imported body's own), weights transferred from the body (closest point, smoothed, four bones) and as animations the walk, idle, turn and raise_arms motions and the captured motions of the project's `motions/` folder; `preset` godot, unity or unreal sets the defaults and names. Metres, Y up. Uses the cached drape from `simulate` if it is up to date. Returns the path, each LOD's triangles and the animations.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "GamePreset": {
      "description": "The engine an export is made for.",
      "enum": [
        "generic",
        "godot",
        "unity",
        "unreal"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "Sides": {
      "description": "How the cloth's back is drawn.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "double_sided",
          "description": "One surface, its material drawn from both sides.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "shell",
          "description": "An inner surface `thickness_mm` inside, facing inwards, and a rim\nalong the pieces' edges; a one-sided material.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Export the draped garment for a game engine.",
  "properties": {
    "animations": {
      "default": true,
      "description": "With `skin`, the avatar's motions as animations (default true).",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "avatar": {
      "default": false,
      "description": "Include the avatar's body (default false).",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "lods": {
      "description": "Levels of detail as ratios of the full triangle count: the first\n1, then decreasing, above 0, at most five (default from the preset:\n1, 0.5, 0.2; Unreal 1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125).",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "normal_map": {
      "description": "Size of the baked normal maps (pixels a side): 0 for none, or a\npower of two from 256 to 4096 (default from the preset: 1024,\n2048 for the engines).",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": [
        "integer",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "path": {
      "description": "Output path relative to the project folder. Defaults to\n`exports/<project name>-<preset>.glb`.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "preset": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/GamePreset",
      "default": "generic",
      "description": "`generic` (default), `godot`, `unity` or `unreal`: sets the\ndefaults below and the names."
    },
    "sides": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Sides",
      "default": "double_sided",
      "description": "`double_sided` (default) or `shell`."
    },
    "skin": {
      "default": true,
      "description": "Skin the garment to the avatar's skeleton (default true; refused\nfor a body without one).",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "thickness_mm": {
      "description": "The shell's thickness (mm, 0.2–20, default 1).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ExportGame",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `export.dxf`

Export all panels as DXF-AAMA (ASTM D6673, ASCII DXF in mm), for pattern and cutting software: one block per piece with its cutting line, sewing line, turn points, notches, grainline, internal lines and name. With `sizes`, a graded nest: every piece once per size, with a `Size:` text. Returns the written path.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Export the pattern as DXF-AAMA.",
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "description": "Output path relative to the project folder. Defaults to\n`exports/<project name>.dxf`.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "sizes": {
      "description": "Sizes of the range to export, by name: one size alone, or several\nnested (a graded nest). Default: the pattern as drawn (base size).",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ExportDxf",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `import.pattern`

Import the pieces of a pattern drawn elsewhere, from a DXF-AAMA (or plain DXF), SVG or PDF file inside the project folder: outlines (curves fitted back to editable edges), seam allowances, notches, grainlines, internal lines and names. A tiled PDF's pages are put back together. One undo step (`pattern.import`). Returns the new panels, what was left out, and the scale: `file`, `given` or `assumed` (check the size when assumed). A Seamly2D (.sm2d) or Valentina (.val) pattern is drafted with its measurement file (the one it names, next to it, or `measurements`) and becomes a garment that can be drafted again for other bodies and sizes (`pattern.import_parametric`); it returns the garment and panels, the pieces left out and the drafting steps not supported.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "UnitSpec": {
      "description": "What one unit of an imported drawing is.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "enum": [
            "mm",
            "cm",
            "m"
          ],
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "in",
          "description": "Inch.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "pt",
          "description": "Point, 1/72 inch.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "px",
          "description": "CSS pixel, 1/96 inch.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Import a pattern from a DXF-AAMA, SVG, PDF, Seamly2D or Valentina\nfile.",
  "properties": {
    "measurements": {
      "description": "A parametric pattern's measurement file, relative to the project\nfolder. By default the one the pattern names, looked for next to\nit.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "page": {
      "description": "PDF: import only this page (1 = first). By default every page,\nwith the tiles of a tiled pattern put back together.",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": [
        "integer",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "path": {
      "description": "The file, relative to the project folder (`r3d import` and the app\ncopy files into `imports/`). Its extension gives the format:\n`.dxf`, `.svg`, `.pdf`, or a parametric pattern `.sm2d` (Seamly2D)\nor `.val` (Valentina).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "scale": {
      "description": "Size factor for a drawing at another scale (e.g. 2 for a pattern\ndrawn at half size). Default 1.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "units": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/UnitSpec"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "What one unit of the drawing is, when the file says nothing or says\nit wrong: `mm`, `cm`, `m`, `in`, `pt` or `px`."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "path"
  ],
  "title": "ImportPattern",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `import.measurements`

Read a Seamly2D or Valentina measurement file inside the project folder (.vit, .smis, .vst, .smms): the avatar takes its height, bust, waist and hips, its other measurements become variables, and a multisize file's sizes become the size range. One undo step (`avatar.use_measurements`). Returns the body, the sizes and the number of variables.

```json
      "type": "string"
    }

  "required": [
    "path"
  ],
  "title": "ImportMeasurements",
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `avatar.import`

Drape on a body imported from an OBJ, glTF, GLB, PLY or STL file inside the project folder (a scan, a game character; you own its licence). Units, up axis and facing are detected unless given (correct them with avatar.orient); the arrangement points are guessed (move them with avatar.set_point) and the measurements taken on the body. One undo step (`avatar.import_mesh`). Returns the measurements and the check (as avatar.check). Imported bodies move with the motions.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "UpAxis": {
      "description": "An axis of a model file.",
      "enum": [
        "y",
        "z",
        "x",
        "-y",
        "-z",
        "-x"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Drape on a body imported from an OBJ, glTF, GLB, PLY or STL file.",
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "description": "The file, relative to the project folder (`r3d avatar import` and\nthe app copy files into `avatars/`): `.obj`, `.gltf` (buffers\nembedded), `.glb`, `.ply` or `.stl`.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "scale": {
      "description": "Metres per file unit; detected when omitted.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "turn_deg": {
      "description": "Turn about the vertical (degrees) so the body faces +Z; detected\nwhen omitted.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "up": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/UpAxis"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The file's up axis (`y`, `z`, `x`, `-y`, `-z`, `-x`); detected\nwhen omitted."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "path"
  ],
  "title": "AvatarImport",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

```json
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "width_mm": {
          "description": "Usable fabric width (mm, 300–3000); omitted: the garment's fabric\nwidth, else 1500.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "PaperSpec": {
      "description": "Page layout of a PDF export.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "a4",
          "description": "A4 tiles to print at home.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "letter",
          "description": "US Letter tiles to print at home.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "single",
          "description": "One page as large as the pattern (plotter, print shop).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "PieceQuantity": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "How many times a piece is cut in a marker, and how.",
      "properties": {
        "count": {
          "default": 1,
          "description": "Copies per size (0–50; 0 leaves the piece out). Default 1.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "free_grain": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "The piece has no grain to follow (felt, interfacing, a bias\npiece): it may lie at every 45°.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "pairs": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Every second copy is turned over (a left and a right).",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "panel": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "panel"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Export a marker as SVG or PDF at 1:1.",
  "properties": {
    "format": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/MarkerFormat",
      "default": "svg",
      "description": "`svg` (default) or `pdf`."
    },
    "marker": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/MarkerSpec",
      "default": {},
      "description": "What to lay out, and on what (as in marker.compute)."
    },
    "paper": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/PaperSpec"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "PDF pages: `single` (default, one page as long as the marker, for\na plotter), `a4` or `letter` tiles."
    },
    "path": {
      "description": "Output path relative to the project folder. Defaults to\n`exports/<project name>-marker.<ext>`.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ExportMarker",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `export.techpack`

Write the project's tech pack as a PDF (landscape A4 or Letter): pictures of the garment, colourways (each garment's colour and fabric), the bill of materials (each garment's fabric with weight, width and price, the fabric one garment takes from its marker in the sample size, and by size when graded; trims), the measurements (size chart, every piece's length along the grain, width, sewing line, areas, allowance and mass, and by size), the pattern to scale, and the sewing notes (every seam with its sides' lengths, ease, gathering; the garments' notes). Returns the path and the fabric per garment.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "TechPackImage": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "A picture to put in the tech pack.",
      "properties": {
        "caption": {
          "description": "Written under it; omitted: none.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "path": {
          "description": "A PNG file inside the project folder (a render, a photo).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "path"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "TechPackPaper": {
      "description": "Page size of a tech pack (landscape).",
      "enum": [
        "a4",
        "letter"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Write the project's tech pack as a PDF.",
  "properties": {
    "images": {
      "description": "Pictures of the garment (PNG files in the project folder), shown\nside by side first. The CLI and the MCP server render a front\nand a back view of their own before these (`views`).",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/TechPackImage"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "labels": {
      "additionalProperties": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "description": "The words of the file, by key (see `docs/specs/23-production.md`;\n`decimal` is the decimal separator). Omitted ones are in English.",
      "type": "object"
    },
    "paper": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/TechPackPaper",
      "default": "a4",
      "description": "`a4` (default) or `letter`, landscape."
    },
    "path": {
      "description": "Output path relative to the project folder. Defaults to\n`exports/<project name>-techpack.pdf`.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ExportTechPack",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `fit.report`

How the draped garment fits, read from the cached drape (`simulate` first; says `drape`: simulated or start): per piece its largest and mean strain (% stretch beyond the pattern), the share of its area at or above `threshold_pct` (default 5), its mean gap to the body (mm) and the share touching it; the tight spots (neighbouring cloth at or above the threshold, strongest first, at most 10: piece, peak strain, area in cm², height above the floor in cm, centre on the pattern in mm); and the ease (garment circumference minus body circumference, cm) at the chest, waist and hips and at any `heights_cm`.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "How the draped garment fits.",
  "properties": {
    "heights_cm": {
      "description": "More heights above the floor (cm) to take the tape at, besides the\nchest, waist and hips.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "threshold_pct": {
      "default": 5.0,
      "description": "Strain (%) from which the cloth counts as tight (default 5).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "title": "FitReport",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `fit.tape`

A tape measure on the cached drape: at `height_cm`, the garment's circumference around the body (cloth length along the horizontal cut, folds included), the body's (a tape around its section) and the ease between them (cm); or, at a point `near` on the drape (m), the same for the loop passing there (a sleeve, the body) plus the gap between the cloth and the body there (mm). `closed` is false when the cut does not go round (an open front, a hem): no ease then.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "A tape measure on the drape.",
  "properties": {
    "height_cm": {
      "description": "Height above the floor (cm): the loop around the body there.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "near": {
      "description": "A point on the drape (m, x right, y up, z forward): the loop\nthrough it at its height (a sleeve, the body…), and the gap to the\nbody there.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 3,
      "minItems": 3,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "FitTape",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `fit.length`

A length on the cached drape between two points of it (`from`, `to`, m): straight, along the cloth (the cut through both points across the cloth, the way a tape laid from one to the other goes, folds included) and by tape (that way pulled taut, bridging the folds), in cm. `joined` is false when the cloth does not join them (two garments, an opening between): only the straight length then.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "A length on the drape between two points of it.",
  "properties": {
    "from": {
      "description": "A point on the drape (m, x right, y up, z forward).",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 3,
      "minItems": 3,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "to": {
      "description": "Another point on the drape (m).",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 3,
      "minItems": 3,
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "from",
    "to"
  ],
  "title": "FitLength",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `drape.diagnose`

Where the drape goes wrong and why, read from the cached drape (`simulate` first; says `drape`: simulated or start). Per face: piece, place on the pattern (mm) and on the drape (m), strain (% stretch beyond the pattern), area against the pattern's (below 1: crumpled), signed distance to the body (mm, negative inside; unsigned while the body moves), the nearest other cloth within 10 mm that is not the face's own neighbourhood (a fold or another layer: piece and distance), and the largest gap of a seam at its corners. With `regions` (a disc on a piece's pattern, or a ball on the drape): each region's summary and its faces, the most strained first. Always: counts (faces, particles that are not numbers, particles more than 2 mm inside the body), every seam's largest and mean gap (widest first), the worst faces of the whole drape (most strained, most crumpled, deepest in the body), at most `limit` (default 20) per list, and `replay`: the project version (`fingerprint`), simulated time and motion this drape comes from.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "Region": {
      "description": "Where to look.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "A disc on a piece of the pattern: its faces whose centre lies\nwithin `radius_mm` of `at_mm` (the piece's coordinates, base size,\nas `fit.report` gives its tight spots).",
          "properties": {
            "at_mm": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "pattern",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "panel": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
            },
            "radius_mm": {
              "format": "double",
              "type": "number"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "panel",
            "at_mm",
            "radius_mm"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "A ball on the drape: its faces whose centre lies within\n`radius_mm` of `point_m` (m, x right, y up, z forward, as\n`fit.tape` takes its points).",
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "drape",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "point_m": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 3,
              "minItems": 3,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "radius_mm": {
              "format": "double",
              "type": "number"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "point_m",
            "radius_mm"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The diagnostic report of the drape.",
  "properties": {
    "limit": {
      "default": 20,
      "description": "Faces listed per list (1–200, default 20).",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "regions": {
      "description": "Regions to report on; omitted: the whole drape.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/Region"
      },
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "title": "DrapeDiagnose",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `library.list`

The pattern library: `builtin`, the built-in patterns (each a template: its id, English title and kind; add one with template.apply), and `patterns`, the user's own saved with library.save (name, kind, folder, and the template it was drafted from if any; add one with library.add). Kinds: tops, bottoms, dresses_and_skirts, accessories, children.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The built-in patterns and the user's own.",
  "title": "LibraryList",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `library.add`

Add a pattern of the user's library (see library.list) to the project as a new garment, worn over the others, drafted again for the avatar (pattern.add: pieces drafted from a template, a Seamly2D/Valentina pattern or formulas follow the body, the others come as drawn; graded in a size range). Its print image is copied into textures/. One undo step. Returns the garment, then the panels and seams.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Add a pattern of the user's library to the project.",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "description": "The pattern's name in the library.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "name"
  ],
  "title": "LibraryAdd",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `library.save`

Save a garment to the user's pattern library, shared by every project, under a name and a kind (tops, bottoms, dresses_and_skirts, accessories; default tops): its pieces, seams, notches, internal lines, construction details, trims, constraints, fabric, colour, print, notes and grading, with the body it is drafted for. A name already in the library is refused unless `replace`. Returns the pattern as library.list lists it.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "GarmentId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a garment, e.g. `garment:1`.",
      "pattern": "^garment:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "PatternKind": {
      "description": "What a pattern is, to sort the library.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "enum": [
            "tops",
            "bottoms",
            "dresses_and_skirts",
            "accessories"
          ],
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "children",
          "description": "Babies' and children's clothes.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Save a garment to the user's library.",
  "properties": {
    "garment": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/GarmentId"
    },
    "kind": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PatternKind",
      "default": "tops",
      "description": "What it is, to sort the library."
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "Its name in the library.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "replace": {
      "default": false,
      "description": "Replace the library's pattern of that name, if there is one.",
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "garment",
    "name"
  ],
  "title": "LibrarySave",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `library.rename`

Rename a pattern of the user's library. Returns it as library.list lists it.

```json
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
```

Delete a pattern of the user's library (projects it was added to keep their garments). Cannot be undone: requires "confirm": true.

```json
    "confirm": {
      "default": false,

    }

    "name"

  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `library.export`

Pack a pattern of the user's library into a zip file in the project folder (default exports/<name>.zip), to share it; library.import adds it to a library. Returns the written path, relative to the project folder.

```json
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Pack a pattern of the user's library into a zip file, to share it.",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "path": {
      "description": "Output path relative to the project folder. Defaults to\n`exports/<name>.zip`.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "name"
  ],
  "title": "LibraryExport",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `library.import`

Add a pattern packed with library.export (a zip file in the project folder) to the user's library; it takes a numbered name when its own is taken. Returns it as library.list lists it.

```json
    "path"
  ],
  "title": "LibraryImport",
  "type": "object"
}
```
